pairs.subject: job-coordination
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/extract/breaker.ts:75 The run status is a closed union, but it is assigned directly at about six sites in the context, and the retry door moves the terminal states `done` and `failed` back to a live stage, so verdicts are not final and no single transition door checks or records why the status moved.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/extract/breaker.ts:75 ExtractStatus (types.ts:196) is closed, but there is no transition door. Direct `m.status =` writes sit in breaker.ts:30, spend.ts:55, performFinish, setStage, store.ts:450 and here. Terminal exits are not empty (done/failed go back to a live stage), and no actor or reason token is written with a transition.

lib/foundry/extract/performReplica.ts:71 A replica round makes a paid generate, writes the file, then suspends on a second vendor call. The manifest is saved only after the whole unit (perform.ts:59). A destruction during the critique leaves the paid pixels on disk but missing from the record, and the m.spend booking is lost, so a re-run pays again. One save after round.file is set would make that state durable.

lib/foundry/extract/lease.ts:18 The legacy manifest lease that the ledger still reads for pre-L29 runs has a TTL sized to the longest unit's duration (generate plus recognise), was renewed per unit rather than on a timer, and is not fenced. The live fenced slot lease is in the kernel, outside this context.

lib/foundry/extract/engine.ts:14 The executor holds a renewable, fenced kernel slot lease, and units are bounded. None of the technique's preconditions (no spare slot, foreign holder, unbounded duration) holds, and nothing in the context probes a pid.

lib/foundry/extract/units.ts:21 Position is derived from the manifest, a total-state record rewritten after every unit, keyed by stable source, style and round ids. Image files are written before the manifest save, so a crash re-runs at most one unit. Resume needs nothing but the manifest. The re-run cost of a paid generate is not declared per step in this context.

lib/foundry/extract/perform.ts:23 The advance call takes no deadline or budget and returns the unit performed (or null when settled or stopped) with the durable status. Time limits sit on the vendor calls.

lib/foundry/extract/store.ts:450 The commit's side effect (one style-store transaction, idempotent on retry per the comment at store.ts:443-444) runs before the terminal `committed` write, so nothing irreversible happens after the verdict. passDeath (performCommon.ts:36) also keeps a process death from being recorded as a vendor failure. Boot sweeps belong to the kernel and were not judged here.

lib/foundry/extract/performRead.ts:26 Run terms (rounds, target, seed, grouping, generator) are clamped and frozen into the manifest at creation (helpers.ts:58-70). The generator is read back from the run's own record at the call (store.ts:290). Every readback and critique is stamped with the vocabulary version it was produced under.
